items.title: Exact pin of `numpy==1.26.4` overwrites Slicer's bundled NumPy

findings.title: Exact pin of `numpy==1.26.4` overwrites Slicer's bundled NumPy
findings.evidence:
base_packages = [
            "numpy==1.26.4",
            "scikit-image==0.22.0",
        ]
        for package in base_packages:
            self.log(f'Installing {package}...')
            slicer.util.pip_install(package)
findings.explanation: `setupPythonRequirements` forcefully installs exact pinned versions `numpy==1.26.4` and `scikit-image==0.22.0` into Slicer's shared Python environment. `numpy` is bundled with 3D Slicer; replacing or downgrading Slicer's bundled `numpy` (especially in newer Slicer releases that use Python 3.12+ or NumPy 2.x, or while `numpy` C-extensions are already loaded in memory) can corrupt Slicer's Python environment and break Slicer core modules or other installed extensions.
findings.suggestion: Do not install or pin `numpy` (rely on Slicer's bundled `numpy` and add `'numpy'` to `packagesToSkip`), and avoid hard-pinning `scikit-image==0.22.0` unless strictly necessary (or use a minimum version constraint like `scikit-image>=0.22.0` only if not already satisfied).

findings.title: Apply pins and can downgrade Slicer's bundled NumPy
findings.evidence:
# Step 1) Install base dependencies first
        # To avoid repeated uninstall/install of packages, we specify exact versions of some packages
        base_packages = [
            "numpy==1.26.4",
            "scikit-image==0.22.0",
findings.explanation: The Apply handler invokes this setup before segmentation. On a Slicer installation with a different NumPy version, pip may replace the shared bundled package, breaking Slicer or other extensions, including in later sessions. The installation happens even before checking whether PyTorch is available.
findings.suggestion: Do not pin or replace Slicer-bundled NumPy; use compatible dependencies or isolate the inference environment from Slicer's Python.

claude.reason: CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:995-1001 runs slicer.util.pip_install('numpy==1.26.4') and 'scikit-image==0.22.0' unconditionally in setupPythonRequirements, which Apply calls (line 387). There is no check of the installed version. numpy is bundled with Slicer. The pin therefore downgrades or replaces it on any Slicer build that ships a different version, for example NumPy 2.x. The policy explicitly lists exact pins of Slicer-bundled packages as a request-changes item. It runs on Apply, not at import. On a Slicer that already ships 1.26.4 it is a no-op.

gpt.reason: CADSWholeBodyCTSeg/CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:993-1001 contains `"numpy==1.26.4",` and `slicer.util.pip_install(package)`, before the PyTorch check at lines 1016-1024. Apply calls setup at lines 385-388. On an installation with another NumPy version, pip may replace the shared package; it need not replace an already matching installation. This is a serious shared-environment compatibility risk and the security policy requests a fix for exact pins of bundled packages, but actual breakage on a particular Slicer version was not demonstrated, so I rate the finding major rather than blocking.

gemini.reason: In `CADSWholeBodyCTSeg/CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:995-1001`, `setupPythonRequirements` explicitly runs `slicer.util.pip_install("numpy==1.26.4")` (and `scikit-image==0.22.0`) on every first run of the session. Under the review rubric and AGENTS.md policy ("Request changes for: ... Downgrading or exactly pinning packages that Slicer bundles (such as numpy, scipy, SimpleITK, pydicom, requests, vtk)"), replacing Slicer's bundled `numpy` with an exact pin can break Slicer's core environment and other extensions.

items.title: First Apply installs dependencies without asking for confirmation

findings.title: First Apply installs dependencies without asking for confirmation
findings.explanation: Clicking Apply immediately starts package installation and shared-environment changes, including the CADS archive and its dependencies when absent. There is no confirmation before this installation path; a status message after starting is not consent to downloads or changes.
findings.suggestion: Before modifying the environment, explain the packages and download size and obtain explicit confirmation; allow cancellation without changes.

claude.reason: onApplyButton (lines 385-388) sets a wait cursor and calls setupPythonRequirements() directly. That function pip-installs numpy, scikit-image and acvl_utils (lines 995-1014). It also downloads CADS from GitHub and installs its dependencies and TPTBox (lines 1053-1087). The only confirmation prompt is for updating an already-installed CADS (lines 1046-1049). A first install gets no consent dialog. The install is user-triggered by Apply, not at import or startup, so I rate it major rather than blocking.

gpt.reason: CADSWholeBodyCTSeg/CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:362-388 calls `self.logic.setupPythonRequirements()` directly when Apply is clicked. Lines 993-1001 run `slicer.util.pip_install(package)`; lines 1051-1064 install CADS when absent without an initial-install confirmation. The confirmation at lines 1043-1049 is limited to updating an existing CADS package from a different URL, and the one at 399-403 concerns a restart after an error. Apply is described as `Start segmentation` at lines 217-221, not as consent to change shared packages. CADS installation is conditional on reaching it, including passing the earlier PyTorch check.

gemini.reason: In `CADSWholeBodyCTSeg/CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:385-388`, `onApplyButton` directly calls `self.logic.setupPythonRequirements()` without prompting the user for confirmation before downloading and installing multiple Python packages into Slicer's environment (note that confirmation is only asked on lines 1046-1048 when upgrading an already-installed CADS package from a different URL, not on initial installation). While installing on `Apply` is much better than installing at module import/startup, installing large dependency trees without user confirmation is a minor/moderate issue.

items.title: Selective dependency installer does not prevent transitive overwrites of Slicer-bundled packages or `numpy`/`scipy`

findings.title: Selective dependency installer does not prevent transitive overwrites of Slicer-bundled packages or `numpy`/`scipy`
findings.explanation: `pipInstallSelectiveFromURL` strips `packagesToSkip` (`SimpleITK`, `torch`, `requests`, `nnunetv2`, etc.) from CADS's top-level `METADATA`, but then installs each remaining requirement (and `TPTBox==...` at line 1087) via normal `slicer.util.pip_install(...)` without `--no-deps` and without excluding `numpy`, `scipy`, `vtk`, or `SimpleITK`. Transitive dependencies (such as `TPTBox` or `monai`/`nibabel`/`scipy`) can still pull or downgrade `torch`, `SimpleITK`, `numpy`, or `scipy` from PyPI into Slicer's shared environment.
findings.suggestion: Include `'numpy'` and `'scipy'` in `packagesToSkip` and pass constraints or check installed packages before calling `pip_install` so transitive dependencies of `CADS` and `TPTBox` cannot overwrite Slicer's bundled packages (`SimpleITK`, `numpy`, `scipy`, `requests`) or PyTorch.

claude.reason: pipInstallSelectiveFromURL (lines 871-892) skips only the names in packagesToSkip. It calls slicer.util.pip_install(requirement) on each remaining requirement, with no --no-deps and no exclusion of numpy, scipy or vtk. Line 1087 installs TPTBox==version the same way. TPTBox's own dependencies are not filtered, so a transitive pull or downgrade of bundled packages is possible. I did not verify what TPTBox actually requires. The skip list does cover torch, SimpleITK, requests and nnunetv2 at the top level only.

gpt.reason: The lack of transitive protection is real: CADSWholeBodyCTSeg/CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:871-892 filters direct requirements with `skipThisPackage = any(requirement.startswith(pkg) for pkg in packagesToSkip)` but then calls `slicer.util.pip_install(requirement)` without `--no-deps`. Lines 1028-1035 list packages skipped only at that level; lines 1085-1087 independently run `slicer.util.pip_install(f"TPTBox=={required_version}")` with dependency resolution enabled. Thus transitive requirements are not constrained by the skip list and can change shared packages. The actual external CADS/TPTBox dependency metadata and a particular resulting downgrade were not available to verify, so the named downstream replacements remain conditional risks, not demonstrated outcomes.

gemini.reason: In `CADSWholeBodyCTSeg/CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.py:872-892` and `1086-1087`, `pipInstallSelectiveFromURL` filters `packagesToSkip` (`SimpleITK`, `torch`, `requests`, `acvl-utils`, `nnunetv2`, `TPTBox`) from CADS's top-level metadata, then installs each remaining requirement (and later `TPTBox=={required_version}`) via `slicer.util.pip_install(...)` with full dependency resolution. Because `packagesToSkip` neither blocks `numpy`/`scipy`/`vtk` at the top level nor constrains transitive dependencies (for example `TPTBox` and other packages depend on `SimpleITK`, `torch`, `numpy`, `scipy`, etc., or pinned versions in CADS's `METADATA`), `pip` can still overwrite or downgrade Slicer-bundled packages or pull `torch`/`SimpleITK` if version specifiers conflict.

findings.evidence:

            self.ui.targetsList.addItem("CADSWholeBodyCTSeg package needs to be installed first.")

items.title: Inference output blocks the GUI thread while awaiting lines

findings.title: Inference output blocks the GUI thread while awaiting lines
findings.explanation: Apply calls this synchronous reader after launching CADS. While inference emits no output, readline blocks the UI event loop, potentially making Slicer unresponsive for the lengthy inference interval.
findings.suggestion: Use asynchronous process notifications or a worker thread and provide responsive progress and cancellation.

                cadsCommand=["echo", "test"]

items.title: Self-test `CADSWholeBodyCTSegTest` has mismatched expectations and will fail

findings.title: Self-test `CADSWholeBodyCTSegTest` has mismatched expectations and will fail
findings.evidence:
# test input arg setting
            defaultParameters = {
                "CPU": "false",
                "UseStandardSegmentNames": "true",
                "Task": "551",  # by default
                "TargetMode": "subset"
            }            
            self.assertIn("551", self.logic.tasks)
            self.assertEqual(self.logic.tasks["551"]["title"], "Core organs")            
            for parameter, defaultValue in defaultParameters.items():
                self.assertEqual(
                    parameterNode.GetParameter(parameter) or "",
                    defaultValue,
                    f"Parameter {parameter} default value incorrect"
                )
findings.explanation: In `setDefaultParameters` (line 1131), `TargetMode` is initialized to `"all"`, whereas `test_Logic` asserts that the default value of `TargetMode` is `"subset"` (and the `.ui` file has `subsetTargetsRadio` checked by default). In addition, `test_ErrorHandling` (lines 1712-1729) expects `logic.process` to raise a `ValueError` for an invalid subset, which `logic.process` does not implement. As a result, the self-test fails.
findings.suggestion: Align the default `TargetMode` between `setDefaultParameters`, `CADSWholeBodyCTSeg.ui`, and `CADSWholeBodyCTSegTest`, and update `test_ErrorHandling` to match the actual behavior of `logic.process`.

findings.title: `UnboundLocalError` on `segmentationNodes` when `logic.process()` fails
findings.evidence:
with slicer.util.tryWithErrorDisplay("Failed to compute results.", waitCursor=True):
            # Create initial segmentation node if needed
            if not self.ui.outputSegmentationSelector.currentNode():
                self.ui.outputSegmentationSelector.addNode()

            self.logic.useStandardSegmentNames = self.ui.useStandardSegmentNamesCheckBox.checked

            # Process and get all created nodes
            segmentationNodes = self.logic.process(
                self.ui.inputVolumeSelector.currentNode(),
                self.ui.outputSegmentationSelector.currentNode(),
                self.ui.cpuCheckBox.checked,
                self.ui.taskComboBox.currentData,
                subset=subset
            )

            # Update UI with first node
            if segmentationNodes and len(segmentationNodes) > 0:
                self.ui.outputSegmentationSelector.setCurrentNode(segmentationNodes[0])

        self.ui.statusLabel.appendPlainText(
            f"\nProcessing finished. Created {len(segmentationNodes)} segmentation nodes."
        )
findings.explanation: In `onApplyButton`, `self.ui.statusLabel.appendPlainText(f"\nProcessing finished. Created {len(segmentationNodes)} segmentation nodes.")` is outside the `with slicer.util.tryWithErrorDisplay(...)` block. Because `tryWithErrorDisplay` catches exceptions and suppresses them after showing an error dialog, if `self.logic.process(...)` raises an exception, `segmentationNodes` is unbound and line 432 raises an unhandled `UnboundLocalError`.
findings.suggestion: Indent the `self.ui.statusLabel.appendPlainText(...)` call so it is inside the `with slicer.util.tryWithErrorDisplay(...):` block.

items.title: Downloaded model weights are under non-commercial license (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)

findings.title: Downloaded model weights are under non-commercial license (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)
findings.evidence: The model weights released in the Releases section of this repository are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).
findings.explanation: The extension code is licensed under Apache 2.0 (`LICENSE`), which permits distribution. However, the pretrained model weights downloaded at runtime are licensed under CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (`LICENSE_MODEL` and `README.md`), restricting model usage to non-commercial/research purposes. Users in clinical or commercial settings should be aware of this restriction.
findings.suggestion: Consider noting the CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 non-commercial model license in the module's `helpText` or `acknowledgementText` inside Slicer so users see it without having to visit the GitHub repository.

findings.title: Model weights carry non-commercial terms
findings.evidence:
The model weights released in the Releases section of this repository are licensed under the Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International License (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

This licensing reflects the inclusion of training data with non-commercial restrictions.
findings.explanation: The stated license permits redistribution under conditions but limits commercial use; the README also calls the weights research-only while describing clinical workflows. Users should be made aware of these restrictions before downloading or using the model.
findings.suggestion: Surface the model terms and intended-use limitations in the module before model download or inference.

items.title: Large screenshot PNG files (~3.7 MB total) committed to repository root

findings.title: Large screenshot PNG files (~3.7 MB total) committed to repository root
findings.evidence:
Screenshot_01.png  (1847577 bytes, binary)
Screenshot_02.png  (1828461 bytes, binary)
findings.explanation: Two large PNG screenshots (~1.85 MB and ~1.83 MB, ~3.7 MB total) are committed directly to the root of the source repository. While not installed by CMake, storing multi-megabyte screenshots in the main git history bloats repository clones.
findings.suggestion: Consider compressing the screenshots or hosting them in a separate documentation branch/release asset.
